title: Lesson 9: Quality at Scale: Golden Sets, Eval Gates, and Regression Discipline
description: Keeping a running delivery correct at volume with a golden set treated as living reference data, eval gates placed where they stop the wrong change, and regression discipline that triages a failing gate instead of burying it.

questions.question: Why must a quality system at scale run both a gate and a sample?
options: A gate catches regressions caused by a change, while a sample catches drift
A gate catches drift over time, while a sample catches change-driven regressions
A gate replaces the golden set, while a sample replaces the need for a gate
A gate screens each live output, while a sample audits the golden set's cases
questions.explanation: A change-triggered gate and a human sample of the live stream cover opposite failures: what a change broke and what drifted with no change at all. Running only one leaves half the estate unverified.

questions.question: When a golden set case fails, what is the correct first response?
options: Rewrite the expected output to match what the system currently does so the gate turns green
Remove the failing case from the set so it stops blocking the planned release
Decide whether the system regressed or the world changed before touching it
Lower the pass bar slightly until the failing case passes again
questions.explanation: The set holds the quality bar, so a failure is a question to answer, not a bar to move. Moving the expected output to match the system deletes the record of what correct used to be.

questions.question: A failing gate is triaged as one of three diagnoses. Which set is correct?
options: A real regression, a stale reference, or a flaky test, each needing its own fix
A real regression, a capacity shortage, or a billing error, each needing its own fix
A blocked run, an expired key, or a delivery failure, each needing its own fix
A scope issue, a schedule issue, or a provider issue, each needing its own fix
questions.explanation: Naming the diagnosis is the whole skill because the fix differs: fix the system for a regression, update the case for stale reference, repair the test for a flaky gate.
